notes: πρὸς τὸ δεῖν is analysed under rule 61: πρός takes the whole clause-introducer *to the end that* headed on *to*, the nominalizing article is unrepresented, and δεῖν keeps *ought*.
αὐτούς is the expressed accusative subject of the infinitive and takes *they*; rule 74's supplied-subject case does not arise because the subject is written in Greek.
προσεύχεσθαι and ἐγκακεῖν each keep their own infinitival *to* under rule 7, no conjunction governing those clauses.
